title: Krein fractional domains via full-interval parity and critical weighted traces
summary: A matched Neumann/shifted-Robin adaptation of Grubb yields ordinary boundary layers off s=3/2+2k and weighted H1/2-type conditions at those critical orders.
conditions: Same fixed c>0 constant-coefficient Kc and coupled boundary domain as proof01.
Ordinary Hs_Sob is the L2 Bessel/Sobolev scale on the smooth interval (-1,1).
Use full-interval Nc=-D^2+c and Rc+4=-D^2+c+4 with outward Robin derivative minus value zero; positivity and normal ellipticity checked in proof02.
Apply Grubb only to these uniform-order j=1 local realizations; reduce parity and compare positive scalar shifts before transferring to Kc.
scope: All s>=0 for this smooth constant-coefficient operator. Constants may depend on c and s. Not an arbitrary mixed-boundary theorem, uniform-c estimate, or deletion classification.
content: For s not equal to 3/2+2k, Hc^s consists of f in Hs_Sob with B(f^(2j))=0 for every 2j+3/2<s; norms are equivalent. At s=3/2+2k require these conditions for j<k and integral_(−1,1) (|fe^(2k+1)|^2+|x fo^(2k+1)-fo^(2k)|^2)/(1-|x|) dx finite. Critical norm includes this integral. The full-interval auxiliary operators remove the otherwise unmatched half-interval mixed-order hypothesis. Point evaluation f^(r)(0) is continuous exactly for s>r+1/2; the proof supplies a localized Fourier countersequence at equality. Full named-family density 0<=s<7/2 stays as the existing project theorem.
